Commentary.Commentary: Hope you enjoyed our coverage of this entire tour. England will now face Pakistan on their home turf on 14th July and Sri Lanka will have Australia visiting them on 26th July. Do join us for those exciting contests. Till then, goodbye and take care!

Right, then! That's it from us. England have made a cleansweep and have bulldozed right through this Lankan side. Dominating and clinical are the words that best describe the hosts in this tour. Sri Lanka have a relatively fresh side but it can be argued they could have done better. There are still positives to take for them, for example, their bowling department, especially the pacers, who have impressed. This will be a good learning curve for them.

We've finally come to an end of a long and grueling tour for Sri Lanka. A little fun fact for our readers. In 2014, Sri Lanka won the Test, ODI and T20 series in England. Two years later, England have redeemed themselves. A superb turnaround, wouldn't you say? Shows you that just about anything can happen in the world of this beautiful game.

Man Of The Match, JOS BUTTLER says he is delighted to take the opportunity to open the innings and grab it with both hands. Also says that the wicket was on the slower side as Mathews and Maharoof put some pressure on them early on. Adds that 160 would have been a decent score and he feels that his side were lucky to bowl first as they could get an idea about the wicket. (On captaining the side towards the end) Says that it's good fun to captain the side as the guys take responsibility and that makes the experience better. (On Dawson's debut) Says he bowled brilliantly, that he has some great skills and he executed them well. (On his Test selection) Says that if you are out of the side, you have the hunger to get back in, and he hopes for the best.

With the exception of Angelo Mathews, the Lankan bowlers were not able to get a grip throughout the innings. Mathews took the only two wickets of the innings and kept his economy rate low as well. Another bowler of note, Nuwan Pradeep was brought on quite late and could not make much of a difference as he bowled just 2 overs. Beside the two, there was not much merit for the fielding side, with many missed opportunities and lucky breaks that allowed Morgan to continue his innings. Buttler too was lucky as he edged one to Chandimal which wasn't given out.

Buttler displayed his batting prowess once more, scoring 73 quickly and his unbeaten 114-run partnership with Morgan, allowed the hosts to coast to victory. The clinical performance by the Englishmen ensured the pressure never got to them and the outcome of the match was never in doubt.

England cleansweep the Lankans! It's another win for the hosts as they beat Sri Lanka in the solitary T20I match. Despite the victorious outcome, England got off to a shaky start with Roy getting dismissed for a duck in the very first over. Things began to look a bit dire for them after Mathews picked up Vince's scalp but Morgan's arrival steadied the innings.

OUT! Carelessness costs Vince! Shorter ball on leg, Vince looks to work it down the leg side but misjudges it. The ball flicks off his pads and the keeper collects it. Unaware that the keeper has it, Vince looks to take a run and doesn't return to the crease. The keeper reaches out and removes the bails. The fielding side bursts into appeals and Vince stands there stricken. He knows his mistake and isn't surprised to find out he is dismissed. England off to a shaky start here.
